thread.title: Streaming Service Race Has One Less Competitor As Walmart Drops Plan

author: APARNA NARAYANAN
title: Streaming Service Race Has One Less Competitor As Walmart Drops Plan
text:
Walmart ( WMT ) reportedly dumped plans to launch a new streaming service that was in the works — one of several seeking to challenge the dominance of Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Hulu in subscription video streaming.
X
Walmart abandoned plans for a new streaming product after talks with veteran media executive Mark Greenberg fell apart last year, sources told CNBC .
Instead, the top U.S. retailer will focus on adding more content to its Vudu streaming platform, its 2010 video acquisition. Vudu's movies and shows can be rented or owned.
Greenberg had reportedly talked to Walmart about a separate service targeting average Americans — and is now said to have approached Costco ( COST ), which may have its own plans in the works .
"Vudu has developed a strong platform, and we aim to continue to bring our customers more content, on more devices, at the best possible price," a Walmart spokeswoman told CNBC in an email. Costco did not respond to CNBC's request for comment.
Walmart stock added 0.4% on Netflix, which reported mixed Q4 results and weak guidance , fell 4% late after closing up 0.5%. Amazon finished 0.6% higher.
 Walmart Video Streaming Service Could Be One Of Many A Walmart video streaming service , under the retailer's Vudu entertainment arm, was first reported in July last year.
Netflix, Amazon Prime Video and Hulu are the main streaming entertainment competitors in the space.
But companies from Apple ( AAPL ) and AT&T ( T ) to Costco and Disney ( DIS ) are preparing or mulling entries in the ultracompetitive subscription video space.
In just the past week, TV broadcaster Sinclair Broadcast Group ( SBGI ) launched just such a streaming service, called Stirr, while NBC Universal announced a 2020 launch for its free streaming service.
